newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Strike deal seen halting fall in Sri Lanka stocks.
newsitem.headline: Strike deal seen halting fall in Sri Lanka stocks.

text.p: The settlement of a six-day strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group should halt a two-day slide in share prices, brokers said on Wednesday.

"News that the strike was settled should arrest the fall to some extent," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, manager institutional sales at Commercial Stock Brokers. "The market was on a correction anyway. News of the strike worsened the situation."
The Colombo Stock Exchange all-share closed 5.3 points down at 625.6 on Tuesday. The strike at Shell Gas Lanka Ltd was called off only after the market closed.
The strike stopped gas supplies to the country, hitting manufacturing stocks like Dankotuwa Porcelain and Ceylon Glass Company.
Rohan Fernando, a broker at CT Smith Stock Brokers, said the market was likely to consolidate on news that the strike was over.
Turnover on Tuesday was 17.4 million rupees, up from Monday's 7.7 million, but well below the average turnover of the month, brokers said.
